thread:
sara_ml: Quick update — brought up skylark-10b (int6) on dev cluster. Raw perf looks promising: ~18% lower cost/token vs our 13b-int8 baseline. Throughput up, latencies down, but we’re seeing a small regression in hallucination rate on long-form summarization slices (>1024 tokens). Sharing microbench and a short proposal.

ben_platform: Nice, can you paste microbench numbers and the exact config? batch sizes, seq len, kv settings? :eyes:

sara_ml: Config: model=skylark-10b, quant=int6, batch=8, seq=2048, kv_warmstart=true. Microbench (dev single-GPU): p50 token latency 82ms (was 98ms on 13b-int8), p95 180ms (was 210ms), throughput 265 tok/s (was 225 tok/s). Cost delta: ~-18% per-token.

tom_eval: What metric are we using for hallucination detection and what prompts?

sara_ml: Eval used RQA-v2 (exact match + entailment scoring). Flag threshold set at 0.85 for pass. Fails cluster on factual anchors and chain-of-thought style summarization that require citation. Example failing prompt: `Summarize this 3k-word customer support thread and list all action items with sources.`

anya_prod: Product note — longform summarization is a high-value vertical for GTN. Even modest hallucination uptick could affect trust. Do we have a unit-econ estimate for a hybrid fallback (skylark default + 13b fallback for risky slices)?

ben_platform: Back-of-envelope: skylark-int6 saves roughly $0.011 per 1k tokens vs 13b-int8 for our infra profile. If we route 10% of long requests to 13b, net savings drops from 18% to ~9% overall (depends on request length distribution). Need slice distribution to refine.

lia_sre: Ops question — any OOMs or memory cliffs at seq=2048? Also will quant profile require a new kernel build for dedicated nodes?

sara_ml: No OOMs observed in dev runs. KV cache usage increased with longer seq; we capped local KV entries to 4096 to keep memory stable. Quant kernels look compatible with our runtime, but we should pin the quant profile and run a short dedicated smoke job before prod.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy initiated for skylark-int6 -> dev (build 20260321.3).

tom_eval: I'll run a targeted eval: 5k longform samples (mix of support threads, docs, and articles) + RQA-v2 + 300 human spot-checks. ETA ~48h. Will report precision/recall and delta vs 13b-int8.

anya_prod: If the eval looks good, we need a GTN-facing one-pager: expected savings, fallback policy, known failure modes, and suggested predicates (e.g., mm_len>1024 || QA_score<0.9 -> route to 13b-int8).

sara_ml: Agreed. I’ll draft a concise scorecard with: microbench table, unit-econ per 1k tokens, fallback routing policy, and a short list of failing prompt patterns. Will share in #eng-ml when ready. :thumbsup:

ben_platform: One more ask — include a simulation of monthly $ impact for typical customer slices (small, medium, long). That helped leadership last time.

sara_ml: Will do. TL;DR proposal (for now): default skylark-int6 for <=512 tokens, skylark-int6 with post-nli filter for 512–1024, and for >1024 run RQA; if RQA <0.9 then fallback to 13b-int8. This should salvage ~80% of the savings while protecting high-value long-form UX.

lia_sre: Thanks — I’ll queue the canary smoke on dedicated after tom_eval results.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy completed (build 20260321.3) — no immediate errors reported.

tom_eval: Uploading partial results tomorrow morning; will include per-slice econ projection and a short list of representative failure cases for the GTN doc.

anya_prod: Great — thanks everyone.
